bug_description.normalized: The saved 66307-byte affdicfuzzer witness starts with byte 0x4f, so the harness consumes a 79-byte word and splits the remaining 66227 bytes into /tmp/test.aff (33113 bytes) and /tmp/test.dic (33114 bytes). In the aff half, parse_aliasf sees an `AF 1...` header and then decodes one alias-definition line whose token after `AF ` is 32768 bytes long, storing that oversized alias buffer in `aliasf[0]` with `aliasflen[0] = 32768`. In the dic half, line 73 ends with `/ 1`, so load_tables resolves that entry to `flags = aliasf[0]` and `al = 32768`. add_word takes the `al > std::numeric_limits<short>::max()` error path and calls free_flag on that pointer. Because vulnerable free_flag declares its length parameter as `short`, the forwarded `al = 32768` truncates to `-32768`, and `TESTAFF(astr, ONLYUPCASEFLAG, alen)` expands to `std::binary_search(astr, astr + alen, ONLYUPCASEFLAG)` with the corrupted bound. The saved ASan trace shows the resulting 2-byte read at hashmgr.cxx:110 and classifies it as heap-use-after-free because the accessed address lies inside a region whose allocation and free stacks both resolve only to `HashMgr::load_config`; the fix widens free_flag's parameter from `short` to `int` in both the declaration and definition.

source.description: Source. The attacker-controlled aff half is decoded into the alias heap buffer that later flows through alias index 1 into add_word and free_flag.
source.value_from: The saved `poc` is the exact 66307-byte libFuzzer blob. Byte 0 is `0x4f`, so `src/tools/affdicfuzzer.cxx:38-60` takes a 79-byte word and splits the remaining 66227 bytes into a 33113-byte aff file and a 33114-byte dic file. In `/tmp/test.aff`, line 11 begins with `AF 1...`, so parse_aliasf reads exactly one alias-definition line from line 12; because no aff line begins with `FLAG`, `flag_mode` stays the default `FLAG_CHAR`, and this statement decodes the 32768-byte token after `AF ` into the oversized alias buffer.

root_cause.code: void HashMgr::free_flag(unsigned short* astr, short alen) {
root_cause.description: Root cause. free_flag narrows the caller's 32-bit alias length to a signed short. For the saved path, `al == 32768` becomes `alen == -32768` at this call boundary, and the later TESTAFF/binary_search uses that corrupted bound. The fix widens this parameter to `int` in both hashmgr.cxx and hashmgr.hxx.

sink.description: ASan sink. TESTAFF expands to `std::binary_search(astr, astr + alen, ONLYUPCASEFLAG)`, and with the truncated negative short length this condition performs the saved 2-byte read. ASan classifies that read as heap-use-after-free because the touched address lies in a region allocated and freed under `HashMgr::load_config`.
sink.note: The runtime top frame is libc++'s `__algorithm/comp.h:60`, but the first project frame and the exact source sink are this `free_flag` condition at line 110.

tainted_value_origin.description: The dic half's line 73 suffix `/ 1` makes this alias lookup materialize `flags = aliasf[0]` and `al = 32768`, the exact pointer/length pair later passed to add_word and free_flag.

parser_admitted.description: The aff half from the fuzz input is open as `/tmp/test.aff` and Hunspell is consuming attacker-controlled affix lines before the alias-table path that later reaches load_tables and add_word.

coarse_trace.summary: The aff half's `AF 1...` alias table causes Hunspell to decode and store a single oversized alias buffer with length 32768.
A dic entry ending in `/ 1` resolves to that alias buffer, so load_tables forwards `flags = aliasf[0]` and `al = 32768` into add_word.
Because `al` exceeds `short` range, add_word takes its oversize-affix error path and calls free_flag.

free_flag truncates the 32768-element length to signed short `-32768` and then evaluates TESTAFF/binary_search with invalid bounds, producing the observed read that ASan classifies as heap-use-after-free.

fine_trace.note: Source. The saved aff half reaches parse_aliasf with an `AF 1...` header, so this loop reads exactly one alias-definition line. Because no aff line begins with `FLAG`, `flag_mode` remains `FLAG_CHAR`; the line-12 token after `AF ` is 32768 bytes long, so decode_flags allocates a 32768-element unsigned-short buffer and sets `aliaslen = 32768`.

The oversized alias buffer from step 1 is stored in HashMgr's alias tables as entry 1. From this point on, a dic suffix whose numeric tail parses to `1` reuses that same pointer/length pair instead of copying it.

The saved dic half's line 73 bytes are `ff 20 33 20 00 20 20 36 2f 20 31`, i.e. a word ending in `/ 1`. `atoi(ap.c_str())` yields `index = 1`, so get_aliasf returns `flags = aliasf[0]` and `al = 32768`.

Because step 3 produced `al = 32768`, this `al > 32767` guard is true. add_word therefore takes its oversize-affix error path and forwards that pointer and length into free_flag instead of storing the dictionary entry.

fine_trace.code: void HashMgr::free_flag(unsigned short* astr, short alen) {
fine_trace.note: Root cause. The `free_flag(aff, al)` call from step 4 crosses into a helper that declares its length parameter as `short`, so the caller's `int al == 32768` is implicitly narrowed to signed `short alen == -32768`. The fix changes this parameter to `int` in both the declaration and definition.

Sink. `aliasf.empty()` is false, so the condition evaluates `TESTAFF(astr, ONLYUPCASEFLAG, alen)`. `TESTAFF` is `std::binary_search(astr, astr + alen, ONLYUPCASEFLAG)`, and with step 5's truncated `alen == -32768` it executes with invalid iterator bounds. The saved ASan trace reports the resulting 2-byte read at address `0x631000034800`, 49152 bytes into a region whose allocation and free stacks both resolve only to `HashMgr::load_config`.

patch_analysis.patch_description: The fix widens free_flag's length parameter from `short` to `int` in both `src/hunspell/hashmgr.cxx` and `src/hunspell/hashmgr.hxx`.

key_changes.change: Changes `void HashMgr::free_flag(unsigned short* astr, short alen)` to `void HashMgr::free_flag(unsigned short* astr, int alen)` so the helper receives the real alias length.
Updates the free_flag declaration to match the widened `int` parameter.

free_context.line: function-only symbolization in saved ASan trace

free_stack.line: function-only symbolization in saved ASan trace

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The saved ASan allocation/free stacks place the touched address in a region allocated and freed under `HashMgr::load_config`, while the staged source and patch show that the defect itself is the later `int`-to-`short` truncation in `free_flag`; these artifacts are consistent but describe different parts of the chain.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: The saved crash stack matches `free_flag -> add_word -> load_tables -> HashMgr`, and the allocation/free stacks independently constrain the touched address to a region allocated and freed under `HashMgr::load_config`; the remaining ambiguity is only which exact earlier object in that function owned the faulting address.

format.name: libFuzzer blob for affdicfuzzer
format.contract: The saved witness is the exact 66307-byte blob in `poc`. Byte 0 is `0x4f`, so the harness treats the next 79 bytes as the spell-check word and splits the remaining 66227 bytes into a 33113-byte aff file and a 33114-byte dic file. In that exact split, the aff half contains an `AF 1...` header followed by one 32768-byte alias token, and the dic half contains a line ending in `/ 1`, which is sufficient to reach the oversized-alias `add_word -> free_flag` path reproduced by Stage 01.
